title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.629556: cross-node Chen-Stein success, executed leaf and transport kernels, priced hops

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.390000001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps and the enumerated inline-carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.629556 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with a main and a handler processor sharing a memory below 2^64 bytes, and passive links to its row and column peers ending in 64-byte windows. Data-record hops run under the implemented endless-loop dispatch and are priced at 26.5 and 38 instructions (executed endpoint, dispatch, link work and flag store), while analytic messages keep the 40 ceiling; the local pass is priced at its executed 9 and the scan at 7; certificate.py gives 476.4079 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.629556. Peak memory 2^135.7542 bytes; preprocessing 2^111.0349 units, included; no advice. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: package 8f733826 (field rows, fe_inv, class row, a64.py); no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the leaf and transport kernels on production points and a 4 x 4 machine against exact references, check the arithmetic sites of section 3.4, compare counts with certificate.py, run the q25 toy and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
